title: A psychoacoustical approach to resolving office noise distraction

findings.mechanism: Psychological factors account for a larger portion of variance in annoyance than physical noise intensity.

limitations: The size of effect for most psychological and personal variables was smaller than anticipated, likely due to the survey being carried out across a range of workplaces rather than in a controlled laboratory setting with uncontrolled extraneous factors.
The study involved “real world" research, dependent on responses from a range of acoustic environments, where sound levels were not controlled.
In real-world settings, noise is one of many confounding variables, potentially obscuring the subtle effects of other factors like personality.
The survey sample size was constraining, and additional research is needed to further test the hypothesis.
